findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0 anonymous website restriction
findings.body: website_name is derived from user_profile.website and added to the public attribute list, but it was not added to untrusted_attributes beside website. That list is what makes UserSerializer omit website, bio, and location when Guardian#restrict_user_fields? is true, i.e. an anonymous viewer looking at a trust level 0 user. Nothing AMS actually invokes applies that check to website_name: include_website_name does not call restrict_user_fields?, and it is not a valid include hook (no trailing ?), so include? defaults to true. Logged-out clients therefore receive the website host, and the path as well when the domain heuristic matches, in the user JSON. The profile template renders model.website_name whenever it is present, so the external URL is shown on the profile even though the raw website attribute is stripped. That undoes the control that kept new accounts from advertising links to anonymous visitors and API clients.

findings.title: Same-site check shows paths for unrelated hosts and hides them for www
findings.body: website_name appends URI#path only when it decides the website host is the same site as Discourse.current_hostname, but the comparison is incorrect. The branch at line 144 treats two hosts as the same whenever they have an equal label count greater than 2 and share every label after the first. For a forum at forum.co.uk, forum.com.au, name.github.io, or app.herokuapp.com that matches every other host under that public suffix, so http://unrelated.co.uk/secret is rendered as unrelated.co.uk/secret instead of unrelated.co.uk. The else branch only appends the path when the forum hostname string-ends with "." plus the website host, and the exact-match branch is case-sensitive while URI#host is lowercased. A forum hostname of Example.com with website http://example.com/user therefore fails every branch and the path is dropped. The usual www/apex pair also fails: forum example.com and website http://www.example.com/user displays www.example.com with no path, which is the case this change is supposed to improve. Profiles will expose paths of unrelated sites and still hide paths for the same site.

findings.title: Profile link text stays stale after the website is edited
findings.body: The visible label used to be a controller computed property of model.website (host taken with split, invalidated when website changed). The template now prints the server snapshot model.website_name while href stays bound to model.website. User#save sends the edited website but only copies bio_excerpt back from the PUT response, so the in-memory website_name is left unchanged. Preferences edit that same user model, and the profile reads it without another fetch, so after a website change the anchor text can still show the previous host and path while the link points at the new URL until a full reload.

findings.title: include_website_name is never used as the serializer include hook
findings.body: ActiveModel Serializers emits an attribute unless include_<attribute>? exists and returns false. This method is named include_website_name without the question mark, so it is never called and the website.present? guard is dead. Every UserSerializer payload therefore includes website_name, with null when the website is blank, unlike location and website which are omitted when blank. Renaming this method to include_website_name? without removing it would also override the include_website_name? defined earlier by untrusted_attributes, because the class-body method is defined later, and that would drop the anonymous TL0 check.

findings.title: Specs never assert website_name is hidden or domain-safe
findings.body: The TL0 anonymous example still only expects bio_raw, bio_cooked, bio_excerpt, location, website, profile_background, and card_background to be absent, so it stays green when website_name leaks. The new website_name examples only stub discourse.org, example.com, and forums.example.com against http://example.com/user. They never cover a public-suffix collision such as forum.co.uk versus http://other.co.uk/secret, or example.com versus http://www.example.com/user, which are the cases the matcher gets wrong. The added tests do not catch the bugs in this change.
